This is like His saying, ﴿Am yuridūna kaydan fa-alladhīna kafarū humu al-makīdūn﴾ ("Or do they intend a scheme? But those who disbelieve, they are the ones who will be ensnared by the scheme"). They used to confer secretly in their assemblies and consult together about his affairs (ﷺ). (p-56)

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 43, verse 80:

﴿Am yahsaboon﴾ means: Rather, do they think (﴿Am yahsabun﴾ here carries the sense of "Rather, do they suppose?").

﴿Anna la nasma'u sirrahum﴾ ("that We do not hear their secret"): this is what they have spoken to themselves or to others in a private place.

﴿Najwahum﴾ ("their private conversation"): that is, what they have said among themselves by way of secret consultation (tanajji).

﴿Bala﴾ ("Yes, indeed"): We do hear both of them and are fully aware of them.

﴿Wa rusuluna﴾ ("and Our messengers"): those who keep watch over their deeds and remain with them wherever they are.

﴿Ladayhim﴾ ("with them"): beside them.

﴿Yaktubun﴾ ("they write"): that is, they write down both of these, or they write down everything that proceeds from them of deeds and words, of which what has been mentioned, their secret and their private conversation, is part. The clause is either a conjunction with what "bala" (yes) indicates, or a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: We hear them while Our messengers are writing.

Say (to the disbelievers), i.e., to establish the truth and to alert them that your opposition to them, by not worshipping what they worship of the angels, peace be upon them, is not due to hatred or enmity toward them or toward those they worship, but is rather due to your certainty in the impossibility of what they attribute to them, and upon which they based their worship of them, namely that they are the daughters of Allah, exalted is He.

﴿If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.﴾ That is, "of Him." This is because he, peace and blessings be upon him, was the most knowledgeable of people regarding the affairs of Allah, exalted is He, and of what is permissible for Him and what is not, and the most deserving of observing His rights; and among the duties of honouring a father is honouring his son. In this there is an indication, in the most emphatic and forceful manner, that they are not so (i.e., that the angels are not His children), and an indication of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ strength of conviction and firmness of foot in the matter of monotheism, which is not hidden; along with this is a drawing down of the disbelievers from the rank of obstinacy, as is indicated by the use of "in" (إنْ) in place of "law" (لَوْ), which signifies the impossibility of the antecedent of the conditional. It has been said: "If the Most Merciful had a son, according to your claim, then I would be the first of the worshippers, the monotheists, of Allah, exalted is He." It has also been said: "then I would be the first of those who are disdainful," i.e., those who are averse to Him, or to the idea that He would have a son; from "ʿabida, yaʿbadu" when his nose becomes very disdainful (ʿabida: to be averse, to be disdainful). It has also been said: "in" is a negative particle, i.e., "There was no son for the Most Merciful; I would be the first to say so." It has been read as "wulduⁿ" (وُلْدٌ) as well.

Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ That is: above what they attribute to Him, namely that He has a son. The attaching of the name "Lord" to the greatest and most powerful of bodies is a reminder that they, and the created things within them, being under His dominion (malakut) and lordship (rububiyyah), how could it be imagined that any of them is a part of Him, glory be to Him? And the repetition of the name "Lord" serves to magnify the status of the Throne.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 43, verse 83:

﴿So leave them﴾ alone, since they did not submit to the truth after hearing this clear proof.

﴿To immerse themselves﴾ in their falsehoods.

﴿And to play﴾ in their worldly life, for what they are engaged in, of deeds and sayings, is nothing but a matter of ignorance and play. The jazm (the apocopate, i.e., the jussive mood, a grammatical term meaning the verb's final vowel is dropped) on the verb is because it is the answer to the imperative (jawab al-amr).

﴿Until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾ — that is, the Day of Resurrection, for on that day they will know what they did and what will be done to them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 43, verse 84:

﴿And He it is who is God in the heaven and God on the earth.﴾ The two adverbial phrases (al-zarfan) are connected to the descriptive meaning (al-ma'na al-wasfi) that the august name (al-ism al-jalil) indicates, namely the meaning of being worshipped in truth (al-ma'buddiyyah bi-al-haqq), on the basis of its being exclusive to the One worshipped in truth, as has passed in the explanation of the basmalah (tafsir al-basmalah). It is as if it were said: "And He it is who deserves to be worshipped in both of them." Its verification has already passed in surah al-An'am. It was also read: "And He it is who is Allah in the heaven and Allah on the earth." The returning pronoun (al-raji') to the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) is a subject (mubtada') that has been elided (hudhif) because of the length of the relative clause (tul al-silah) by the connection to the complement of the predicate (muta'allaq al-khabar) and the conjunction (al-'atf) upon it. There is no room (la masagh) for the prepositional phrase (al-jarr) to be a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam) with "ilah" as a delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), because the sentence would then be left without a returning pronoun (li-luzum 'ara' al-jumlah hina'idhin 'an al-'a'id). Yes, it is permissible for it to be the relative clause (silah) of the relative pronoun, with "ilah" being the predicate of an elided subject (khabar li-mubtada' mahdhuf), on the basis that the sentence is an explanation (bayan) of the relative clause, and that His being in the heaven is in the manner of divinity (ʿala sabil al-ilahiyyah), not in the manner of settlement (la ʿala sabil al-istiqrar). In it is the negation of heavenly and earthly deities, and the restriction of the entitlement to divinity to Him, exalted is He. His exalted saying: ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ serves as evidence (ka-al-dalil) for what precedes it.

﴿And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾, either permanently, as with the air, or at some times, as with birds.

﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, that is: the knowledge of the time at which the Resurrection will take place.

﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, for recompense. The shift to the second person (iltifat) serves as a warning (tahdid). It is also read in the third person (ghayba), and "tuhsharun" is read with the letter ta' (in the second person, as "you will be gathered").

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 43, verse 86:

﴿And those whom they invoke do not possess﴾ i.e., whom they invoke (يَدْعُونَهُمْ). It is also read with the ta' (تَدْعُونَ), both lightened and doubled.

﴿intercession, besides Him﴾ as they claim.

﴿except one who bears witness to the truth﴾ which is the Oneness of God (al-tawhid).

﴿and they know﴾ what they bear witness to, with insight, certainty and sincerity. The plural pronoun is used in consideration of the meaning of "one who" (man), just as the singular was used first in consideration of its wording. The exception may be contiguous (muttasil), with the relative pronoun being general to everything worshipped besides God; or it may be disjunctive (munfasil), on the basis that it is specific to the idols.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 43, verse 87:

﴿And if you were to ask them, "Who created them?"﴾ That is: you asked the worshippers and those who are worshipped.

﴿They would surely say, "Allah."﴾ Denial is impossible because its falsehood is at its utmost extreme.

﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾ That is: how are they diverted from His worship to the worship of others, while they acknowledge that all of it is created by Him, exalted is He?

﴿وَقِيلِهِ﴾ (*wa-qīlihi*, "and His saying") is in the genitive (*bi-l-jarr*), either as a conjunction with *al-sā'ah* (the Hour), meaning: with Him is the knowledge of the Hour and the knowledge of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him.

﴿يا رَبِّ﴾ ("O my Lord") ... and so on, because *al-qawl*, *al-qīl* and *al-qāl* are all verbal nouns (*maṣādir*). Or the *wāw* is for oath (*lil-qasam*), and His statement, exalted is He, ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Indeed, these are a people who do not believe"), is its answer. In swearing by it there is elevation of his rank, peace and blessings be upon him, and magnification of his supplication and his turning to Almighty God, which is not hidden.

It has also been read in the accusative (*bi-l-naṣb*), by conjunction with *sirrahum* (their secret), or with *maḥall al-sā'ah* (the place of *al-sā'ah*), or by supposing a verb of its own (*bi-iḍmār fi'lihi*), or by supposing a verb of oath (*bi-taqdīr fi'l al-qasam*). It has also been read in the nominative (*bi-l-rafʿ*) as the subject of a nominal sentence (*ʿalā al-ibtidāʾ*), with the predicate being what follows it. Its conjunction with *ʿilm al-sāʿah* has also been permitted.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 43, verse 89:

﴿So turn away from them﴾: i.e., turn away from their call (da'wah), and despair of their faith.

﴿And say, "Peace"﴾: i.e., my affair is one of taslim (bidding farewell/peace) from you and of leaving you alone (mutarakah).

﴿But they will come to know﴾: their condition definitely, even if that is delayed. This is a warning from God Most High to them, and a consolation to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). It has also been read as "they will know" (taʿlamūn), on the basis that it falls within the scope of "say" (qul).

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Zukhruf will be among those to whom it is said on the Day of Resurrection: 'O my servants, no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve. Enter Paradise without reckoning.'"
